name: The Iron Kettle Taproom
description: A corner spot with brick walls and a big front window. They keep the beer cold and the stools sturdy. Good place to sit with a guitar case and wait for the set to start.

name: Hollow Tree Books
description: Tucked into a ground-floor unit with shelves that go from floor to ceiling. The owner knows every author in the building. They’ll let you read a few pages if you ask nicely.

name: Clay & Canvas Gallery
description: A bright room with white walls and polished concrete floors. Local painters and potters hang their work here. It’s quiet enough to hear yourself think, but lively enough to feel part of the crowd.

name: Morning Freight Coffee
description: A small shop with an espresso machine that hums all day. They serve pastries from the bakery next door. Perfect for grabbing a cup before heading to the next stage.

name: Vinyl Hound Records
description: A narrow store packed with crates of used records. The floorboards creak underfoot. You can browse the jazz section for an hour and no one will rush you.

name: Signal Hall
description: A large room with high ceilings and good acoustics. The stage is low, so you’re close to the musicians. They rent it out for weddings, but tonight it’s for the band.

name: The Crooked Slice
description: A family-run place with red-checkered tablecloths. The pizza comes out hot and cheesy. It’s the kind of place where you eat with your hands and talk loud.

name: Two Flats Bike Shop
description: A workshop with bikes hanging from the ceiling and tools on the wall. They fix flats and tune chains. After the festival, you can park your bike here and know it’s safe.
